title: Which monodromy groups do Jacobian counterexamples have?
premise_risks: The premise that the Jacobian conjecture was refuted in 2026 rests on 2026 preprints (arXiv:2607.20210, 2607.21572, 2608.00222); if those counterexamples fail, the set M is empty and the question changes completely.
arXiv:2608.02863 (Kistner-Shaska, 2026 preprint): source of S_d, A_d (d = 6, 12, families) as realized monodromy groups.
arXiv:2609.33491 (Fonollosa, 2026 preprint): source of imprimitive wreath-type monodromy groups.
plain: A Keller map (polynomial map with constant nonzero Jacobian) that is not invertible covers a generic point d times, and following the d preimages around loops gives a permutation group, its monodromy. Campbell's 1973 theorem says that if this group is regular (the Galois case), the map is invertible. The 2026 counterexamples realize full symmetric groups and some imprimitive groups. Is there a non-invertible Keller map whose monodromy group is primitive but does not contain the alternating group? Further questions (not part of the formal claim): is Campbell's theorem the only obstruction, i.e. does every non-regular transitive group occur?
math: For a Keller map $F:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^n$ ($\det JF\in\mathbb C^\times$) of geometric degree $d$, let $\mathrm{Mon}(F)\le S_d$ be the geometric monodromy group (the Galois group of the Galois closure of $\mathbb C(x)/\mathbb C(F)$ acting on the $d$ embeddings of $\mathbb C(x)$ over $\mathbb C(F)$). It is transitive, and by Campbell's theorem it is regular only if $d=1$. Let $\mathcal M$ be the set of transitive groups (up to permutation isomorphism) arising as $\mathrm{Mon}(F)$ for non-invertible Keller maps in some dimension; $\mathcal M$ contains $S_d$, $A_d$ (e.g. $d=6,12$ and the families of Kistner-Shaska 2608.02863) and imprimitive wreath-type groups (Fonollosa 2609.33491), and is closed under direct products in product action ($F\times G$). Claim: there exist $n$, a non-invertible Keller map $F:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^n$ and a primitive group $H\le S_d$ with $A_d\not\le H$ such that $\mathrm{Mon}(F)$ is permutation-isomorphic to $H$ (necessarily $d\ge5$; candidates: $\mathrm{AGL}(1,p)$ for a prime $p\ge5$, $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ on 7 points). Prove or disprove; a disproof means every primitive member of $\mathcal M$ is alternating or symmetric. Further questions (not part of the formal claim): is $\mathcal M$ exactly the set of non-regular transitive groups? (A disproof of the Claim answers this negatively.)
